speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound confirms a large ovarian mass and significant ascites, which likely explains your shortness of breath due to pressure on the diaphragm. To help determine the nature of this mass and guide treatment, have you noticed any unexplained weight loss, night sweats, or changes in your appetite recently?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, chest pain, or swelling in the legs. She has not noticed any changes in bowel or urinary habits.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will now order tumor markers to help characterize the mass. REQUEST TEST: CA-125

speaker: Doctor
text:
A normal CA-125 level in the presence of a large ovarian mass and ascites is highly suggestive of Meigs syndrome, which is typically associated with an ovarian fibroma. To confirm this diagnosis and rule out other causes, I need to assess your heart function. Do you have any history of heart disease, and are you experiencing any palpitations or chest tightness?

REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal echocardiogram rules out cardiac causes for your symptoms and supports the likelihood of Meigs syndrome, which involves an ovarian fibroma, ascites, and pleural effusion. To fully confirm this, I need to check for fluid in your lungs.

REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of a right-sided pleural effusion completes the classic triad of Meigs syndrome: an ovarian fibroma, ascites, and pleural effusion. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meigs syndrome
